tasks.task_name: Establish core team structure with 4-5 members
tasks.description:
Based on the requirement specification section 6.1, establish the core project team consisting of 4-5 people with the following composition:
- Product Manager (1 person)
- Technical Lead (1 person)
- Backend/CLI Developer (2 people)
- Quality Assurance (1 person)

This task involves identifying, recruiting, or assigning team members to fill each of these roles to ensure the project has the necessary human resources to deliver the MVP. The team structure is hierarchical with the Product Manager and Technical Lead providing leadership, Backend/CLI Developers handling implementation, and QA ensuring quality standards.

parameters.structure:
Project Team (4-5 people)
├── Product Manager (1)
├── Technical Lead (1)
├── Backend/CLI Developer (2)
└── Quality Assurance (1)

tasks.task_notes: This is a foundational task that must be completed early as all other development activities depend on having the appropriate team in place. Consider internal assignments first before external recruitment to accelerate timeline.

requirement_snippets:
### **6.1 Core Team Structure**
```
Project Team (4-5 people)
├── Product Manager (1)
├── Technical Lead (1)
├── Backend/CLI Developer (2)
└── Quality Assurance (1)
```
success_criteria: Team must consist of 4-5 people
Must include exactly 1 Product Manager
Must include exactly 1 Technical Lead
Must include 2 Backend/CLI Developers
Must include exactly 1 Quality Assurance person

tasks.task_name: Define and document Product Manager role
tasks.description:
Per requirement specification section 6.2.1, create comprehensive documentation for the Product Manager role including all specified responsibilities and MVP deliverables.

The Product Manager is responsible for:
- Defining and prioritizing the feature roadmap
- Gathering user requirements and feedback
- Coordinating between stakeholders and the development team
- Managing project timeline and milestones
- Ensuring business requirements are met
- Creating user documentation and marketing materials

The Product Manager must deliver specific MVP artifacts including user stories with acceptance criteria, MVP scope definition, user testing plan, and go-to-market strategy for the CLI tool. This documentation will serve as the basis for performance evaluation and role clarity.

responsibilities: Coordinate between stakeholders and development team

tasks.task_notes: This role definition should be created as a formal document (e.g., in a TEAM_ROLES.md or similar) that can be shared with the assigned Product Manager and used during onboarding. Ensure MVP deliverables are clearly defined with acceptance criteria.

requirement_snippets:
#### **6.2.1 Product Manager**
**Responsibilities:**
- Define and prioritize feature roadmap
- Gather user requirements and feedback
- Coordinate between stakeholders and development team
- Manage project timeline and milestones
- Ensure business requirements are met
- User documentation and marketing materials

**MVP Deliverables:**
- User stories and acceptance criteria
- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
success_criteria: Product Manager role must include all 6 specified responsibilities
Product Manager must deliver user stories and acceptance criteria
Product Manager must deliver MVP scope definition
Product Manager must deliver user testing plan
Product Manager must deliver go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
dependencies: Establish core team structure with 4-5 members

tasks.task_name: Product Manager delivers MVP scope definition

This task involves the Product Manager creating a clear, bounded definition of what will be included in the minimum viable product (MVP) for the CLI tool. The scope definition should identify which features are in-scope vs. out-of-scope, establish MVP boundaries, and set realistic expectations for the initial release.

This document is critical for preventing scope creep and ensuring the team delivers a focused, viable product within the project timeline.
tasks.task_notes: Should be created in close collaboration with the Technical Lead to ensure the MVP scope is technically achievable within the project timeline. This deliverable will inform all subsequent planning and implementation tasks.
